q: A plant disease is usually defined as normal growth. (2025-Set 1)
e: A plant disease is usually defined as abnormal growth.

q: Biotic diseases are caused by non-living environmental conditions. (2025-Set 3)
e: Biotic diseases are caused by living organisms (pathogens).

q: Nematodes are very large roundworms. (2025-Set 10)
e: Nematodes are microscopic roundworms.

q: Study of plant diseases is called plant pathology. (2025-Set 2)
e: The study of plant diseases is called plant pathology.

q: Disease may also promote yield and quality of harvested product. (2025-Set 5)
e: Plant diseases reduce the yield and quality of harvested products.

q: Abiotic diseases are caused by non-living environmental conditions. (2025-Set 11)
e: Abiotic diseases are caused by non-living environmental conditions.

q: Most plant diseases, around 85 percent are caused by bacteria and viruses. (2025-Set 13)
e: Most plant diseases (around 85 percent) are caused by fungi.

q: Disease may also reduce yield and quality of harvested product. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား/2026- Set 1)
e: Diseases reduce the overall yield and quality of harvested crops.

q: Plant disease is any abnormal condition that alters the appearance or function of a plant. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Plant disease refers to any abnormal condition altering appearance or function.

q: Abiotic diseases are caused by living organisms. (2026- Set 2)
e: Abiotic diseases are caused by non-living environmental factors.

q: Chemical injury will likely cause damage on different types of plants. (2025-Set 6)
e: Chemical injury causes damage selectively depending on plant susceptibility and exposure.

q: The fungi that cause tomato leaf blight do not cause damage on sweet corn. (2025-Set 8)
e: Fungi causing tomato leaf blight are host-specific and do not infect sweet corn.

q: Pseudomonas bacteria can cause leaf spot of tobacco, blight of peas and soybeans. (2026-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Pseudomonas bacteria cause leaf spot of tobacco as well as blight in peas and soybeans.

q: Signs of plant disease are physiological evidence of the pathogen. (2024-Set 2)
e: Signs are physical evidence of the pathogen, whereas symptoms are physiological evidence.

q: Nematodes are multicellular animals. (2025-Set 3)
e: Nematodes are multicellular, microscopic roundworms.

q: All plants are attacked by one species or another of phytopathogenic bacteria and viruses. (2024-Set 4)
e: Phytopathogenic bacteria and viruses show host specificity and do not attack all plants indiscriminately.

q: All bacteria are bad for plants and soil. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အများတွင်မေး)
e: Many bacteria are beneficial to plants and soil, such as nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

q: Bacteria are most active in warm and humid environments. (2024-Set 3/2025-Set 4)
e: Warm and humid conditions favor bacterial reproduction and activity.

q: Plant parasitic nematodes have a stylet, a piercing mouthpart. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အများတွင်မေး)
e: Plant parasitic nematodes use a stylet to pierce plant cells and feed.

q: Chemicals used to control fungi are called fungicides. (2025-Set 12)
e: Fungicides are chemical agents specifically formulated to control fungal pathogens.

q: Most cardiovascular disease starts with atheroma formation. (2026- Set 2)
e: Atheroma formation in arterial walls is the starting point for most cardiovascular diseases.

q: Measuring blood pressure is used as an indicator of both the heart and blood vessels. (2026- Set 1)
e: Blood pressure measurements reflect the health status of both the heart and blood vessels.

q: Warfarin and heparin are a class of medicines used to reduce blood clotting. (2026-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Warfarin and heparin act as anticoagulants to reduce blood clot formation.

q: A stroke is caused by an interruption to the normal blood supply to an area of the heart. (2025-Set 12)
e: A stroke occurs when blood supply to an area of the brain is interrupted.

q: A healthy blood pressure is around 120 mmHg during diastole and around 80 mmHg during systole. (2025-Set 11)
e: Healthy blood pressure is around 120 mmHg during systole and 80 mmHg during diastole.

q: Platelet inhibitory drugs such as aspirin are also a type of anticoagulant. (2025-Set 13)
e: Aspirin and platelet inhibitory drugs prevent clotting by inhibiting platelet aggregation.

q: Non-infectious diseases are those that are not caused by pathogens. (2025-Set 10)
e: Non-infectious diseases are caused by environmental, genetic, or lifestyle factors rather than pathogens.

q: The hardening of arteries, caused by atheroma, is called angina. (2025-Set 8)
e: The hardening of arteries caused by atheroma is atherosclerosis; angina is chest pain.

q: Oxygen is supplied to the liver muscle by the coronary arteries. (2025-Set 4)
e: Coronary arteries supply oxygenated blood directly to the heart muscle.

q: DVT is the formation of blood clot in a vein deep outside the body (2025-Set 6)
e: DVT (Deep Vein Thrombosis) is the formation of a blood clot in a vein deep inside the body.

q: Oxygen is supplied to the heart muscle by the coronary arteries. (2024-Set 2, 4)
e: Coronary arteries supply oxygenated blood to the heart muscle.

q: The development of atherosclerosis is linked to many types of cancers. (2024-Set 3)
e: Atherosclerosis is primarily linked to cardiovascular diseases, not cancers.

q: Sedentary lifestyle can lead to heart diseases. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Lack of physical activity in a sedentary lifestyle increases the risk of heart disease.

q: The narrowed coronary arteries supply enough oxygenated blood and the heart muscle resorts to anaerobic respiration. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Narrowed coronary arteries fail to supply enough oxygenated blood, forcing the heart muscle into anaerobic respiration.

q: Most cases of malaria are caused by one of five species of the protist Plasmodium. (2025-Set 9)
e: Malaria in humans is primarily caused by specific Plasmodium species, predominantly Plasmodium falciparum.

q: The parasites enter the white blood cells, where they multiply. (2025-Set 2)
e: Plasmodium parasites enter and multiply within red blood cells (erythrocytes).

q: Plasmodium can also pass across the placenta from mother to foetus. (2025-Set 5)
e: Plasmodium can cross the placental barrier from mother to fetus, causing congenital malaria.

q: Plasmodium multiplies only in single hosts. (2025-Set 1)
e: Plasmodium requires two hosts (mosquitoes and humans/vertebrates) to complete its lifecycle.

q: The best protection against malaria is to avoid being bitten. (2025-Set 7)
e: Preventing mosquito bites is the primary and most effective protection against malaria.
